say: Glitch's crystal vault just cracked open! Twelve power crystals spill out.
Four knights want fair shares. Deal them out, one at a time, round and round.
Every knight gets three. That's fair!
We write it like this: twelve divided by four equals three.
Division means splitting into equal groups!
Division can ask another question. How many bags of three can we fill?
Four bags! So twelve divided by three is four.
Your turn! Fifteen gems, five knights. How many does each knight get?
after: Three each! Deal them out and see.

say: Division is fair sharing. You've got it, knight!
Arf! Next up: the reverse spell!
Twelve magic shields, floating in three rows of four.
Three rows of four. That's a times fact: three times four equals twelve.
Now cast it backwards. Twelve shared into three rows? Four in each row. Twelve divided by three is four.
Twelve into four columns? Three in each. Twelve divided by four is three.
Three numbers, one family. Two times facts and two division facts.
Flip it, and it still works!
That's the reverse spell. Division undoes multiplication.
Stuck on fifty-six divided by seven? Think: seven times what is fifty-six?
Seven times eight! So fifty-six divided by seven is eight.
Use the times facts you already own!
Your turn! Twenty-four divided by six. Think: six times what is twenty-four?
after: Four! Six times four is twenty-four.

say: Every times fact you know is a division fact too.
Glitch's robot guards a heap of gold: eight gold bars and four coins.
Four knights share eighty-four. Start with the big ones: the tens.
Eight tens shared by four: two tens each.
Now the ones. Four coins shared by four: one each.
Two tens and one one. Each knight gets twenty-one!
In long division, the tens answer goes over the tens, and the ones answer goes over the ones.
Tens first, then ones. Big things first!
Your turn! Sixty-nine divided by three. Tens first!
after: Twenty-three! Two tens each, then three ones each.

say: That's how heroes split big numbers.
But what if the tens don't split evenly?
Seventy-two gold: seven bars and two coins. Three knights to share it.
Seven tens shared by three: two each. But one bar is left over!
We can't cut a bar into three... unless we trade it at the forge.
Smash! One ten becomes ten ones.
Ten coins, plus the two we had: twelve ones.
Twelve shared by three: four each.
Two tens and four ones. Twenty-four each!
In long division, that leftover ten shows up when you subtract. Then bring down the two to make twelve.
Your turn! Fifty-two divided by four.
after: Thirteen! One ten each, trade the extra ten, then three ones each.

say: When a ten won't split, trade it for ten ones!
Ellie found fourteen bones. Three puppies want to share them.
Deal them out. Four each... and two left over.
Two bones can't go around three puppies fairly. That's the remainder.
Fourteen divided by three is four, remainder two.
The remainder must be smaller than the number you divide by. Three or more left? Everyone gets another one!
And the leftovers? Ellie has a plan.
Your turn! Seventeen shared by five is three each. How many are left over?
after: Two left over. Seventeen divided by five is three, remainder two.

say: When it doesn't split evenly, the leftover is the remainder.
Every knight learns the code. Four moves, over and over.
Four hundred fifty-six divided by three. Divide: how many threes in four? One.
Multiply: one times three is three.
Subtract: four minus three is one.
Bring down the five. Now we have fifteen.
Your turn! Divide: how many threes in fifteen?
after: Five! Five times three is fifteen. Fifteen minus fifteen is zero. Bring down the six.

say: Threes in six? Two. Two times three, six. Six minus six, zero. Nothing left!
Four hundred fifty-six divided by three is one hundred fifty-two.
Divide, multiply, subtract, bring down. Repeat until you run out of digits!
And a true knight checks. One fifty-two times three... four fifty-six. It matches!
Multiply every digit, even the first!
You know the Knight's Code. Now go split some treasure in the Division Dungeon!
